title.en: Australia politics live: Hume claims Labor’s algorithm bill gives it too much power; embattled developer Bathla stands down 200 workers
title.zh: 新闻直播：澳大利亚冲浪者在墨西哥遇害案父母抵达审判地；工党面临收紧游说规则的压力

summary.en: Follow the day’s news live One Nation proposal to divert super to pay packet One Nation has come up with a plan to give people their superannuation earlier, reducing the amount they’ll have at retirement in exchange for a cash boost. Continue reading...
summary.zh: 关注当日新闻直播：一国党提议将养老金提前发放给民众，以换取眼前的现金注入，但会减少退休时的养老金总额。继续阅读……

body.en:
The government’s proposed digital duty of care legislation , part of its crackdown on social media, gives too much power to the communications minister, the deputy opposition leader, Jane Hume, told the ABC this morning:

We don’t feel that the minister should have the powers to determine what is and is not online harm.

You could understand why there would be a natural suspicion. When the government tries to control the internet, it inevitably fails.

Andrew Bushnell from the Institute of Public Affairs echoed Hume’s claim, quipping that Australians would be trading the algorithm for the “alborithm”.
body.zh: 职业养老金是我国近几十年来的重大改革之一。 它将为数以百万计的澳大利亚人提供退休保障，否则他们将无法获得退休保障。

reflection.en: The proposal to allow early access to superannuation funds, while offering a short-term financial boost, risks diminishing the long-term security intended for retirement. This raises questions about how we balance immediate needs with the responsibility to preserve resources for future generations. Proverbs 13:22 reminds us that a good person leaves an...
reflection.zh: 允许提前支取养老金的提议，虽然能提供眼前的经济援助，却可能损害退休时的长期保障。这引发了如何在平衡当前需求与为后代保存资源的责任之间做出抉择的问题。箴言 13:22 提醒我们，善人给子孙遗留产业，强调了为未来进行管理的重 要性。

verse.textEn: A good person leaves an inheritance for their children's children, but a sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.
verse.textZh: 善人给子孙遗留产业；罪人为义人积存资财。

title.en: Hundreds of far-right protesters descend on Portsmouth after small boat arrival
title.zh: 极右翼抗议者在小船抵达后聚集在朴茨茅斯

summary.en: Coastguard brings asylum seekers to shore as far-right influencer livestreams event calling for men to travel to port. Far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast.
summary.zh: 海岸警卫队将寻求庇护者带到岸边，同时一位极右翼网红正在直播活动，呼吁人们前往港口。极右翼活动家聚集在朴茨茅斯，此前一艘载有140名寻求庇护者的小船在驶向朴茨茅斯海岸时被拦截。

body.en: Influencer livestreams event calling for men to travel to port to block coaches carrying asylum seekers from leaving Hundreds of far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast. The vessel’s arrival sparked a major response with a helicopter, an aeroplane and lifeboats sent to the scene. It is thought to be the first time such a large boat containing asylum seekers has been brought to Portsmouth and the first time a large group of anti-migrant protesters have tried to block newly arrived asylum seekers from being processed. Continue reading...
body.zh: 海岸警卫队将寻求庇护者带上岸，极右翼影响者直播活动呼吁男子前往港口极右活动分子袭击了朴茨茅斯，一艘载有 140 名寻求庇护者的小船在驶向朴茨茅斯海岸时被拦截。此事引起了强烈反响，一架直升机、一架飞机和救生艇被派往现场。据信，如此大的载有寻求庇护者的船只首次被带到朴茨茅斯。船上的乘客已被带到这座海上城市的岸边，并正被长途汽车送往肯特郡拉姆斯盖特郊外的曼斯顿，在那里处理小船的抵达。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Asylum seekers, arriving by boat in Portsmouth, encountered a hostile demonstration. The scene underscores the vulnerability of those seeking refuge and the importance of advocating for the voiceless. Proverbs 31:8-9 calls us to "speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute" and to "defend the rights of the...
reflection.zh: 抵达朴茨茅斯的寻求庇护者在乘船抵达时，遭遇了敌对的示威活动。这一场景凸显了寻求庇护者的脆弱性，以及为无声者发声的重要性。《箴言》31:8-9呼吁我们“为不能自辩的开口，为所有孤苦者伸明正义”和“为穷乏人和贫穷人伸明公理”。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Germany’s far-right AfD thanks Elon Musk as France warns state election win a ‘serious moment’
title.zh: 德国极右翼 AfD 感谢埃隆·马斯克，法国警告州选举胜利是“严肃时刻”

summary.en: The lead candidate for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party in Saxony-Anhalt has thanked Elon Musk following the party's significant victory in a German state election. This win, which saw the AfD more than double its support, positions it to potentially become the first far-right party to hold state...
summary.zh: 德国极右翼选择党（AfD）在萨克森-安哈尔特州选举中取得重大胜利后，该州领先候选人感谢了埃隆·马斯克。此次选举使 AfD 的支持率翻倍，并可能使其成为二战后首个在德国州一级掌权的极右翼政党。一位法国部长称此为欧洲的“严肃时刻”，并强调了历史背景。

body.en: Lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt welcomes further ‘strong’ cooperation with Musk as French minister says ‘We cannot forget our history’ The candidate who led the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party to a historic state election victory in Germany has thanked Elon Musk for his support, as one French minister warned that this was a “serious moment” for Europe. The AfD more than doubled its support in the Saxony-Anhalt region and appears to be on the brink of becoming the first far-right party to gain power in Germany at state level since the second world war. Continue reading...
body.zh: 萨克森-安哈特州首席候选人欢迎与马斯克进一步“强有力”合作，法国部长表示“我们不能忘记我们的历史”这位领导极右翼德国新选择党在德国取得历史性州选举胜利的候选人感谢埃隆·马斯克的支持，一位法国部长警告说，这对欧洲来说是一个“严肃的时刻”。德国选择党在萨克森-安哈尔特地区的支持率增加了一倍多，似乎即将成为二战以来第一个在德国州一级获得权力的极右翼政党。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rise of the AfD in Germany, a party with far-right leanings, marks a significant political shift. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that when the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, people groan. This verse prompts reflection on the character of leadership and its impact on a nation's well-being.
reflection.zh: 德国极右翼选择党（AfD）的崛起标志着重大的政治转变。箴言29:2提醒我们，义人掌权，众民就喜乐；暴徒掌权，百姓就叹息。这节经文促使我们反思领导者的品格及其对国家福祉的影响。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport
title.zh: 亚马逊货运飞机在迈阿密机场坠毁致五人死亡

summary.en: Five people died and five were seriously injured when an Amazon Air Boeing 767-300 cargo plane overran the runway and caught fire during landing at Miami International Airport. The aircraft had departed from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and also impacted vehicles on the ground. The FAA grounded all flights following the...
summary.zh: 一架亚马逊航空的波音767-300货运飞机在迈阿密国际机场降落时冲出跑道并起火，造成五人死亡，五人重伤。该飞机从波多黎各圣胡安出发，并撞击了地面上的车辆。事件发生后，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）下令所有航班停飞。

body.en:
An Amazon Air cargo plane overshot the runway while attempting to land at Miami International Airport, killing five people and seriously injuring five more.

The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft crashed just before 14:00 local time (19:00 GMT) after departing from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The flight also hit several vehicles on the ground.

Amazon said that it is "working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened".

All flights were ordered grounded by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as fire crews raced to the smoking crash site. The crash comes over Labor Day weekend, one of the busiest travel times of the year.

"At least five people have lost their lives, and five others are injured," Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said at a news conference on Sunday evening.

"Right now, our focus is on the families, those who were injured, and the ongoing response," she continued.

Three of the five people injured are in critical condition, said Miami Fire Chief Raied Jadallah. The mayor said they were all taken to hospital with "unknown injuries".

Several of the injured were trapped inside or under vehicles on the ground, and needed to be extricated by fire and rescue crews, said Jadallah.

Officials say it is too early to know the cause of the crash, and that it will be investigated by the National Transportation Safety Board. The federal agency, which investigates all air crashes in the US, plans to hold a news conference on Monday.

The Amazon flight operated by 21 Air, a charter company based in North Carolina, "overran Miami International Airport's diagonal runway and is disabled at the northwest end of the airport," the airport said in a statement.

Miami Dade Fire Rescue said crews "arrived to find an airplane that had caught on fire as a result of this crash, with heavy flames and smoke showing".

Over 200 firefighters responded to the crash. The flames were extinguished, but there is still a fuel leak at the site, said Jadallah.

Amazon issued a statement saying that it is working closely with authorities and offering condolences to the victims.

"We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today's incident at Miami International Airport," said Kelly Nantel, Amazon's Director of Corporate Global Media Relations.

"Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss.

"The airplane, which was operated by 21 Air, was attempting to land when this incident occurred. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to learn more and will cooperate fully with any investigation."

Flight data from tracking site FlightRadar24 shows that the Amazon cargo flight was travelling...
body.zh: 亚马逊航空一架货机在试图降落迈阿密国际机场时冲出跑道，造成五人死亡、五人重伤。 这架波音 767-300 货机于当地时间 14:00（格林威治标准时间 19:00）从波多黎各圣胡安路易斯·穆尼奥斯·马林国际机场起飞后坠毁。飞机还击中了地面上的几辆车。 亚马逊表示，它“正在与地方当局和官员密切合作，以了解到底发生了什么”。 当消防人员赶往冒烟的坠机现场时，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）下令所有航班停飞。事故发生在劳动节周末，这是一年中最繁忙的旅行时间之一。 迈阿密戴德县市长丹妮拉·莱文·卡瓦在周日晚上的新闻发布会上说：“至少有五人丧生，五人受伤。” “现在，我们的重点是家庭、受伤者以及正在进行的反应，”她继续说道。 迈阿密消防队长雷德·贾达拉 (Raied Jadallah) 表示，五名受伤人员中，三人伤势严重。市长表示，他们都被送往医院，伤势“不明”。 贾达拉说，几名伤者被困在地面车辆内或车下，需要消防和救援人员营救。 官员们表示，现在了解事故原因还为时过早，国家运输安全委员会将对此进行调查。负责调查美国所有空难事件的联邦机构计划于周一举行新闻发布会。 迈阿密国际机场在一份声明中表示，这架由北卡罗来纳州包机公司 21 Air 运营的亚马逊航班“冲破了迈阿密国际机场的对角跑道，并在机场西北端瘫痪”。 迈阿密戴德消防救援队表示，工作人员“赶到后发现一架飞机在这次坠机事件中起火，并冒出浓烟和浓烟”。 超过 200 名消防员对事故进行了救援。贾达拉说，火焰已被扑灭，但现场仍有燃油泄漏。 亚马逊发表声明称，正在与当局密切合作，并向受害者表示哀悼。 亚马逊公司全球媒体关系总监凯利·南特尔 (Kelly Nantel) 表示：“得知今天迈阿密国际机场发生的事件中有五人丧生，我们感到非常伤心。” “我们向家人、亲人以及所有受到这一毁灭性损失影响的人表示最深切的同情。 “这架由 21 Air 运营的飞机在事件发生时正试图降落。我们正在与地方当局和官员密切合作以了解更多信息，并将全力配合任何调查。” 来自跟踪网站 FlightRadar24 的航班数据显示，亚马逊货运航班正在飞行......

reflection.en: The suddenness of the crash at Miami International Airport brings a stark reminder of life's fragility. In moments of such profound loss, the biblical promise that Yahweh will wipe away every tear, and death shall be no more, offers a deep and enduring hope beyond the immediate grief. This hope is not a denial of suffering, but a future where all sorrow is...
reflection.zh: 在迈阿密国际机场发生的这起突如其来的坠机事故，令人警醒地提醒我们生命的脆弱。在如此深切的悲痛时刻，《启示录》中雅伟将擦去一切眼泪，不再有死亡的应许，为我们带来了超越眼前伤痛的深刻而持久的盼望。这份盼望并非对苦难的否认，而是指向一个所有忧伤终将得到医治的未来。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Susan Sarandon says she is losing movie roles because of her support for Palestine
title.zh: 苏珊·萨兰德称因支持巴勒斯坦失去电影角色

summary.en: Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon stated that she and other outspoken critics of Israel are finding it 'impossible' to get hired by major studios, with Sarandon herself losing movie roles due to her support for Palestine, despite a perceived shift in public opinion against US support for Israel.
summary.zh: 奥斯卡影后苏珊·萨兰德表示，她和其他批评以色列的知名人士发现，在主要电影公司那里“不可能”获得工作。萨兰德本人也因支持巴勒斯坦而失去了电影角色，尽管她认为公众舆论已转向反对美国支持以色列。

body.en: Oscar-winning actor says she and other outspoken critics of Israel have found it ‘impossible’ to get hired by major studios The Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon has said she is still losing work because of her outspoken support for Palestinians, despite what she ⁠described as a broader shift ⁠in public opinion against ​US support for Israel. Speaking at the Venice film festival, where she is promoting her latest movie The Echo Chamber, Sarandon said some parts of the film industry continued to ⁠shun her over her activism. Continue reading...
body.zh: 奥斯卡获奖演员苏珊·萨兰登 (Susan Sarandon) 表示，她和其他直言不讳的以色列批评者发现“不可能”被大型电影公司聘用。 奥斯卡获奖演员苏珊·萨兰登 (Susan Sarandon) 表示，由于她对巴勒斯坦人的直言不讳的支持，她仍在失去工作，尽管她称公众舆论反对美国支持以色列的情况发生了更广泛的转变。萨兰登在威尼斯电影节上宣传她的最新电影《回音室》，她在发言中表示，电影界的某些部分仍然因为她的激进主义而回避她。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Susan Sarandon's experience of losing work for her outspokenness on Palestine raises questions about the industry's willingness to engage with difficult topics. It prompts reflection on whether public statements of support or criticism are truly valued, or if they become a liability when they challenge prevailing narratives or powerful interests. James 2:15...
reflection.zh: 苏珊·萨兰德因在巴勒斯坦问题上的直言不讳而失去工作，这引发了人们对电影行业是否愿意处理棘手话题的疑问。这促使我们反思，公开的支持或批评是否真正受到重视，或者当它们挑战主流叙事或强大势力时，是否会成为一种负担。雅各书2:15提醒我们，真正的信念常常会受到其后果的考验，敦促我们思考言行背后的实质。

verse.textEn: Suppose a brother or a sister is without clothes and daily food. If one of you says to them, 'Go in peace; keep warm and well fed,' but does nothing about their physical needs, what good is it?
verse.textZh: 若是弟兄或是姊妹，赤身露体，又缺了日用的饮食，你们中间有人对他们说：「平平安安地去吧，愿你们穿得暖、吃得饱」，却不给他们身体所需用的，这有什么益处呢？

title.en: Austria's Islamic headscarf ban in force as under-14s go back to school
title.zh: 奥地利禁止14岁以下学童佩戴头巾的禁令生效

summary.en: As the new school year begins in Austria, a law banning headscarves in schools for girls under 14 has gone into force. The law forbids "traditional Muslim" head coverings, such as hijabs or burkas, in public and private schools across the country. Integration Minister Claudia Bauer, from the conservative People's...
summary.zh: 随着新学年开始，奥地利一项禁止14岁以下女童在学校佩戴头巾的法律已生效。该法律禁止在全国的公立和私立学校佩戴“传统穆斯林”头饰，如希贾布或布卡。保守党（ÖVP）的融合部长克劳迪娅·鲍尔表示，头巾是“压迫的象征，是从幼年时期控制女孩的手段”。但批评者认为，新法律正在助长该国的反穆斯林情绪，并可能违宪。

body.en:
As the new school year begins in Austria, a law banning headscarves in schools for girls under 14 has gone into force.

The law forbids "traditional Muslim" head coverings, such as hijabs or burkas, in public and private schools across the country.

Integration Minister Claudia Bauer, from the conservative People's Party (ÖVP), says the headscarf is "a sign of oppression and a means of controlling girls from the earliest childhood".

But critics say the new law is fuelling anti-Muslim feeling in the country and could be unconstitutional.

The law was brought in by the conservative-led coalition of three centrist parties, the ÖVP, the Social Democrats (SPÖ) and the liberal Neos. They say the law is a "clear commitment to gender equality" and is intended to protect the rights of young girls.

Carla Amina Baghajati, from the official Islamic Community in Austria (IGGÖ), told the BBC that the organisation "firmly opposes the ban".

"We believe it unjustifiably restricts the fundamental right to freedom of religion and disproportionately affects Muslim girls," she said.

"Rather than protecting children, it singles out a specific religious practice and risks excluding the very children it claims to support."

The IGGÖ said it would support legal challenges by girls and their families "who believe that their fundamental rights are being infringed" and who wished to bring their cases before the Constitutional Court.

The court struck down a previous ban on headscarves in primary schools in 2020 on the basis that it contravened the principle of Austria's religious neutrality.

Teachers are expected to enforce the new ban if they see a child wearing a headscarf by holding a series of talks with the student and their legal guardians.

If there are repeated violations, child services must be notified and as a last resort, guardians could face fines of up to €800 (£685).

The Green Party's Sigi Maurer accused Education Minister Christoph Wiederkehr, from the liberal NEOS, of "creating new conflicts and offloading them onto the teachers".

She said teachers were "already under enormous strain" and that Wiederkehr wanted to "foist the role of police officers onto them" on top of their other duties.

The opposition far-right Freedom Party (FPÖ) says the current ban doesn't go far enough. It is calling for a general prohibition on headscarves and face coverings in schools for students and teachers alike.

The FPÖ's Ricarda Berger said there was "no place for political Islam in Austria, and certainly not in our schools".

Austria's Chancellor Christian Stocker, leader of the ÖVP, recently called for a constitutional ban on political Islam, telling Austrian public broadcaster ORF he did not "want to live in an Islamic state".

body.zh: 随着奥地利新学年的开始，一项禁止 14 岁以下女童在学校戴头巾的法律已生效。 该法律禁止全国公立和私立学校戴“传统穆斯林”头饰，例如头巾或罩袍。 来自保守派人民党 (ÖVP) 的融合部长克劳迪娅·鲍尔 (Claudia Bauer) 表示，头巾是“压迫的标志，是从童年开始控制女孩的一种手段”。 但批评人士表示，新法律正在加剧该国的反穆斯林情绪，并且可能违反宪法。 该法律是由三个中间派政党（ÖVP、社会民主党（SPÖ）和自由派新党）组成的保守派领导的联盟提出的。他们表示，该法律是“对性别平等的明确承诺”，旨在保护年轻女孩的权利。 奥地利官方伊斯兰社区 (IGGÖ) 的卡拉·阿米娜·巴加贾蒂 (Carla Amina Baghajati) 告诉 BBC，该组织“坚决反对这项禁令”。 “我们认为，这不合理地限制了宗教自由的基本权利，并对穆斯林女孩造成了不成比例的影响，”她说。 “它不是保护儿童，而是挑选出一种特定的宗教习俗，并有可能将其声称支持的儿童排除在外。” IGGÖ 表示，它将支持“认为自己的基本权利受到侵犯”并希望将案件提交宪法法院的女孩及其家人提出的法律挑战。 2020年，法院撤销了之前在小学佩戴头巾的禁令，理由是它违反了奥地利宗教中立的原则。 如果老师看到学生戴着头巾，他们将与学生及其法定监护人进行一系列谈话，以执行新禁令。 如果屡次违规，必须通知儿童服务机构，作为最后手段，监护人可能面临最高 800 欧元（685 英镑）的罚款。 绿党的西吉·莫雷尔 (Sigi Maurer) 指责来自自由派 NEOS 的教育部长克里斯托夫·维德克尔 (Christoph Wiederkehr)“制造新的冲突并将其转嫁给教师”。 她说，教师们“已经承受着巨大的压力”，维德克尔希望在他们的其他职责之外，“把警察的角色强加给他们”。 反对党极右翼自由党 (FPÖ) 表示，目前的禁令还不够。它呼吁全面禁止学生和教师在学校佩戴头巾和面罩。 自由党的 Ricarda Berger 表示，“奥地利没有政治伊斯兰的容身之地，我们的学校更是如此”。 奥地利总理兼 ÖVP 领导人克里斯蒂安·斯托克 (Christian Stocker) 最近呼吁宪法禁止政治伊斯兰教，他告诉奥地利公共广播公司 ORF，他“不想生活在伊斯兰国家”。 法国已经颁布禁令...

reflection.en: Austria's new law banning headscarves for girls under 14 frames itself as protection, yet critics fear it fosters discrimination. This tension highlights the ongoing challenge of balancing cultural norms with individual rights, and the potential for well-intentioned laws to inadvertently harm the very people they aim to help. The call to 'learn to do right;...
reflection.zh: 奥地利禁止14岁以下女童佩戴头巾的新法律，以保护为名，但批评者担心这会助长歧视。这种紧张关系凸显了在平衡文化规范与个人权利方面持续存在的挑战，以及善意立法可能无意中伤害其意图帮助的人群。‘你们要学习行善，寻求公平，解救受欺压的’（以赛亚书1:17）提醒我们，要审视我们政策对弱势群体的真正影响。

verse.textEn: Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.
verse.textZh: 学习行善，寻求公平，解救受欺压的；给孤儿伸冤，为寡妇辨屈。

title.en: Five killed after Amazon cargo plane barrels off runway, hits vehicles
title.zh: 亚马逊货运飞机冲出跑道撞毁车辆致五人死亡

summary.en: An Amazon cargo plane veered off the runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in five fatalities and three individuals transported to trauma centers in critical condition. The aircraft impacted vehicles upon exiting the runway, leading to a complex extrication process for victims trapped in both the vehicles...
summary.zh: 一架亚马逊货运飞机在迈阿密国际机场冲出跑道，造成五人死亡，三人被送往创伤中心，情况危急。飞机冲出跑道时撞毁了车辆，导致被困在车辆和飞机中的受害者需要复杂的救援工作。

body.en:
An Amazon cargo plane has barrelled off a runway at Miami International Airport, killing at least five people as it struck vehicles and burst into flames.

Miami-Dade County fire chief Ray Jadallah told reporters that in addition to five deaths, three people were transported to trauma centres "in critical condition" and two more were treated at a local hospital.

"The airplane did strike a couple of vehicles" which left "a couple of victims that were actually trapped in the vehicles", Jadallah said.

"A complex extrication with our technical rescue team" was needed, "including a search and rescue of the pilot and co-pilot that were trapped in this aircraft".

Jadallah did not clarify whether the pilot or co-pilot survived, and officials declined to answer questions after brief statements.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Video showed thick smoke billowing from the blue and white Boeing 767 that had arrived around 4am AEST Monday from Puerto Rico, as fire trucks raced to the scene.

The plane operating as Prime Air Flight 7598 caught fire as a result of the "crash", fire officials said.

"A total of 60 fire apparatuses arrived, just short, just shy of 200 men and women from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, to begin the actual search and rescue and firefighting," Jadallah said.

"The actual cause of the incident will be determined by the FAA and the NTSB," he added, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board.

The NTSB said in an X post on Sunday that the B-767-300 cargo aeroplane was flying into Miami from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and it has "launched a go team to investigate Sunday's runway excursion accident".

The airport closed all runways and taxiways due to the incident and posted an update on its website that travellers should check directly with their airline before heading to the airport.

Amazon put out a statement saying the aircraft "experienced an incident while attempting to land". It did not say if anyone was hurt or killed.

"This is a fast-moving situation and we're still gathering details. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened," Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in the statement.

Miami sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz told reporters Sunday that her officers encountered a "really tragic scene," but there was "no apparent threat to public safety".

body.zh: 一架亚马逊货机冲出迈阿密国际机场跑道，撞上车辆并起火，造成至少五人死亡。 迈阿密戴德县消防队长雷·贾达拉告诉记者，除了五人死亡外，三人被送往创伤中心，“情况危急”，另有两人在当地一家医院接受治疗。 贾达拉说，“飞机确实撞上了几辆车”，导致“几名受害者实际上被困在车里”。 需要“我们的技术救援队进行复杂的救援”，“包括对被困在这架飞机中的飞行员和副驾驶进行搜救”。 贾达拉没有澄清飞行员或副驾驶是否生还，官员们在简短声明后拒绝回答问题。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 视频显示，澳大利亚东部标准时间周一凌晨 4 点左右从波多黎各抵达的蓝白色波音 767 冒出滚滚浓烟，消防车迅速赶往现场。 消防官员称，这架Prime Air 7598航班的飞机因“坠机”而起火。 贾达拉说：“迈阿密戴德消防救援队总共派出了 60 辆消防车，不到 200 名消防队员，开始实际的搜救和灭火工作。” 他补充说：“事件的实际原因将由美国联邦航空局和国家运输安全委员会确定。”他指的是联邦航空管理局和国家运输安全委员会。 NTSB 周日在 X 帖子中表示，这架 B-767-300 货机正从波多黎各圣胡安飞往迈阿密，并已“组建了一个调查小组来调查周日发生的跑道偏离事故”。 由于该事件，机场关闭了所有跑道和滑行道，并在其网站上发布了更新，称旅客在前往机场之前应直接与航空公司联系。 亚马逊发表声明称，这架飞机“在试图着陆时发生了事故”。它没有说是否有人受伤或死亡。 亚马逊发言人凯利·南特尔在声明中表示：“情况瞬息万变，我们仍在收集细节。我们正在与地方当局和官员密切合作，以了解到底发生了什么。” 迈阿密警长罗西·科尔德罗-斯图茨周日告诉记者，她的警员遇到了“真正悲惨的场景”，但“公共安全没有明显受到威胁”。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

In moments of such profound loss, we are drawn to the biblical promise that Yahweh will wipe away every tear, and there will be no more death or mourning, pain, or suffering, for...
reflection.zh: 迈阿密国际机场亚马逊货运飞机坠毁的突发事件，夺走了五条生命，另有数人伤势危重，这是对生命脆弱性的严峻提醒。在如此深切的失落时刻，我们被吸引到雅伟的圣经应许：他要擦去一切眼泪，不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛，因为以前的事都过去了。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'
title.zh: 冒生命危险扑灭印度尼西亚“碳炸弹”野火的志愿者

summary.en: Peat fires in Borneo are releasing ancient stores of carbon, causing toxic smog to spread across Southeast Asia. Volunteer firefighters are risking their lives to combat these fires using basic tools.
summary.zh: 婆罗洲的泥炭火正在释放古老的碳储存，导致有毒烟雾扩散到整个东南亚。志愿者消防员正冒着生命危险，使用基本工具与这些火灾作斗争。

body.en:
The sky grows heavy in Borneo, though not with rain. The air, amber-hued and treacle-thick, is smudged under a blanket of smog that has spilled across international borders – to Singapore, Manila, Kuala Lumpur.

"It hits your nose straight away, your eyes burn – that's more or less what it's like," he says. "People say these fires are extraordinary because of the flames and the smoke. And they're right."

The 35-year-old volunteer firefighter has spent more than a month enveloped in this haze, breathing toxic millennia-old microparticles of carbon as he toils against a seemingly inextinguishable fire front.

Using hand tools, carts and portable fire pumps, he and thousands of other volunteer firefighters – many of them indigenous Dayak or Banjar people – are up against an inferno that has carbonised some 200,000 hectares of forest and farmland across Indonesian Borneo since early July.

Underground and out of sight, giant subterranean peat fires continue to smoulder, choking the air with poisonous fumes.

"Once a fire becomes uncontrolled, it harms many people. Not just humans, but also animals and plants," Sujatmoko says. "If underground fire spreads and can no longer be controlled, the losses are enormous."

Amid a so-called "Super El Niño" that has supercharged local drought conditions, thousands of active fire hotspots are spreading and multiplying across the country, fuelling a transnational haze crisis that is the region's worst in more than a decade.

But what makes Borneo's fires particularly worrying is the fact that they are burning through one of the world's largest tropical peatland ecosystems.

This 4.5-million-hectare swathe of forest and swamp, under normal conditions, serves as a valuable reservoir for ancient carbon.

When these peatlands catch fire, they risk releasing millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane into the atmosphere – a "pulse" of greenhouse gas emissions that has earned them the sobriquet of "carbon bomb".

"Peatlands are incredibly effective carbon stores because their waterlogged conditions slow decomposition, allowing carbon to accumulate underground for thousands of years," explains Dr Nisa Novita, a peatland researcher at Indonesian conservation NGO Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara (YKAN).

"But this also means they can become a 'carbon bomb' when they are drained or burned, because that carbon can be rapidly released into the atmosphere.

"Tropical peatlands in Indonesia are among the world's most effective natural carbon stores. The deeper the peat, the greater the carbon stock – and in Kalimantan, we have found peat deposits that can exceed 20 metres in depth."

A peatland that deep has been known to harbour more than 6,000 tonnes of carbon – roughly equivalent to the annual CO₂...
body.zh: 婆罗洲的天空变得阴沉，尽管没有下雨。琥珀色、浓稠的空气被烟雾笼罩着，烟雾已经跨越国际边界蔓延到新加坡、马尼拉、吉隆坡。 “它直接击中你的鼻子，你的眼睛会被灼伤——或多或少就是这样的感觉，”他说。 “人们说这些火灾非同寻常，因为火焰和烟雾。他们是对的。” 这位 35 岁的志愿消防员已经在这片薄雾中度过了一个多月，在看似无法扑灭的火锋中奋力奋战，呼吸着有毒的千年碳微粒。 他和其他数千名志愿消防员（其中许多是土著达雅克人或班贾人）使用手动工具、手推车和便携式消防泵，对抗自 7 月初以来已使印度尼西亚婆罗洲约 20 万公顷森林和农田碳化的大火。 在看不见的地下，巨大的地下泥炭火继续闷烧，有毒烟雾使空气窒息。 “一旦火灾失控，就会伤害很多人。不仅是人类，还有动物和植物，”苏加特莫科说。 “如果地下火势蔓延且无法再控制，损失是巨大的。” 在所谓的“超级厄尔尼诺”现象加剧了当地干旱的情况下，数千个活跃的火灾热点正在全国范围内蔓延和繁殖，加剧了该地区十多年来最严重的跨国雾霾危机。 但婆罗洲的火灾尤其令人担忧的是，它们正在烧毁世界上最大的热带泥炭地生态系统之一。 在正常条件下，这片 450 万公顷的森林和沼泽是宝贵的古代碳库。 当这些泥炭地着火时，它们面临着向大气中释放数百万吨二氧化碳、一氧化碳和甲烷的风险——这种温室气体排放的“脉冲”为它们赢得了“碳炸弹”的绰号。 印度尼西亚保护非政府组织 Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara (YKAN) 的泥炭地研究员尼萨·诺维塔 (Nisa Novita) 博士解释说：“泥炭地是非常有效的碳储存库，因为它们的浸水条件会减缓分解速度，使碳在地下积累数千年。” “但这也意味着它们在被排干或燃烧时可能会变成‘碳炸弹’，因为碳会迅速释放到大气中。 “印度尼西亚的热带泥炭地是世界上最有效的天然碳储存库之一。泥炭越深，碳储量就越大，在加里曼丹，我们发现了深度超过 20 米的泥炭沉积物。” 据了解，这么深的泥炭地蕴藏着超过 6,000 吨的碳——大约相当于每年的二氧化碳排放量……

reflection.en: The volunteer firefighters in Borneo are battling not only flames but also the toxic haze from millennia-old carbon stores. Their relentless effort, day after day, in the face of overwhelming conditions speaks to a deep well of resilience. Like those who wait for Yahweh, they find strength to continue their arduous work, even when exhausted, in the hope of...
reflection.zh: 婆罗洲的志愿者消防员不仅在与火焰搏斗，还在与千年古老碳储存释放的有毒烟雾作斗争。他们日复一日、在压倒性的条件下不懈的努力，体现了深厚的韧性。正如那些等候雅伟的人一样，即使筋疲力尽，他们也能找到力量继续艰苦的工作，希望能最终得到解脱和更晴朗的天空。

verse.textEn: Those who hope in Yahweh will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary.
verse.textZh: 但那等候雅伟的，必从新得力。他们必如鹰展翅上腾。

title.en: Germany's far-right AfD set for big win in eastern state, just short of majority
title.zh: 德国极右翼在东部州大获全胜——预测

summary.en: Germany's AfD party is projected to win over 44% of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, significantly outpacing the conservative CDU. The party has declared the result "historic" and aims to govern, marking a notable electoral success for the far-right in post-WWII Germany.
summary.zh: 根据预测，德国选择党（AfD）有望在东部萨克森-安哈尔特州赢得超过44%的选票，远超保守的基督教民主联盟（CDU）。该党已宣布这一结果是“历史性的”，并寻求执政，这标志着二战后德国极右翼在选举中取得了显著成功。

body.en:
Germany's Alternative for Germany (AfD) is heading for a dramatic victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, far ahead of its mainstream rivals. Although it is projected to fall short of a majority, the AfD says it has won a mandate to govern.

The far-right AfD is on course to win a record 44% of the vote, well ahead of the conservative CDU on 17%, with most interim results counted.

Charismatic leader in the state, Ulrich Siegmund, said it was "sensational" and they wanted to start governing as soon as possible.

No far-right party has won control of a German state since World War Two, and governing at state level would mean powers over policing, local education and culture.

Saxony-Anhalt has a small population of 2.1 million and the AfD in the state is assessed by domestic intelligence as "right-wing extremist", a classification rejected by Siegmund, 35.

He along with joint national leaders Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla were overjoyed as exit polls revealed they were on track to score more than double the party's result in 2021.

Commentators and political opponents spoke of the outcome as a watershed and break with the past. Main TV channel Das Erste cancelled its legendary crime drama Tatort to focus on what the result meant.

"This isn't just about Saxony-Anhalt," Siegmund told supporters. "It's a signal for the whole of Germany - a self-confident signal."

US President Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the German TV projection on his Truth Social platform, and then Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev took a screengrab of Trump's post and praised a "historic win for the pragmatic AfD".

Dmitriev had earlier praised the Russia-friendly AfD as "the party of hope and reason, co-operation truth and hope for Germany". Ahead of Germany's federal election last year, US Vice-President JD Vance endorsed the party, in a move criticised in Germany as political interference.

Polish centre-right Prime Minister Donald Tusk saw the result very differently, saying "in Poland only idiots and traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD".

Without enough seats to form a majority government, Ulrich Siegmund has so far refused to lead a minority government, even though the party's national leaders see it as a possibility.

"If necessary there'll just be new elections, then we'd just get 50 or 55%," said Siegmund, while saying he was prepared to work with individual MPs or a party.

For hours it was unclear whether the BSW would reach the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament, although interim results showed it had succeeded. Had it failed, then the AfD would have seen its chances of a majority increase.

The AfD is currently heading for 39 seats in the 83-seat state parliament instead of the 42 needed for an outright majority.

body.zh: 根据初步预测，德国选择党将在东部萨克森-安哈尔特州取得重大胜利，远远领先于其主流竞争对手。目前尚不清楚这是否足以在该州掌权，但选择党表示它已赢得了执政授权。 极右翼政党将赢得超过 44% 的选票，远远领先于保守派基民盟 (CDU) 的 18.4%。 德国选择党称赞这一结果是“历史性的成果”，而该州富有魅力的领导人乌尔里希·西格蒙德拒绝与任何其他政党一起执政。 自第二次世界大战以来，没有一个极右翼政党赢得了德国一个州的控制权，州一级的治理意味着对治安、地方教育和文化的权力。 萨克森-安哈特州人口很少，只有 210 万，该州的德国选择党被国内情报机构评估为“右翼极端分子”，齐格蒙德拒绝接受这一分类。 德国选择党的预计结果高于早期民意调查显示的结果，西格蒙德以及联合国家领导人爱丽丝·韦德尔和蒂诺·克鲁帕拉在消息传出后欣喜若狂。 然而，政党领导人在看到哪些小党进入州议会之前，不会知道他们是否有足够的席位来执政。 这可能取决于其中一个较小的政党是否超过了 5% 的要求。 如果民粹主义左翼 BSW 未能加入，那么选择党获得多数席位的机会就会增加。 当屏幕上出现投影时，德国选择党选举之夜党总部的一群支持者爆发出欢呼声。 “我们在这个州创造了历史，”齐格蒙德说。他在基民盟中的对手斯文·舒尔茨承认获胜，并表示他的政党将不得不应对这一结果：“这是一场极其艰难和激烈的竞选活动。” 德国中左翼社民党称这一结果“真正具有戏剧性”，而与基民盟一起执政的国家领导人拉尔斯·克林贝尔则称这一结果是“向柏林发出的信号”。 AfD 代表德国另类选择 (Alternative für Deutschland)。它不仅主导了竞选活动，而且正在成为结果的主导力量。尽管结果最初并不清楚，但该党的支持者相信他们正在游行。 萨克森-安哈尔特州的投票率尤其高，估计达到 78%，马格德堡的选择党支持者赞扬齐格蒙德在赢得选民方面的成功。 “无论哪个政府，他们都只是承诺事情会变得更好。这是劳动人民的政党。这是德国的替代方案，”他告诉英国广播公司。 其他政党拒绝与选择党结盟，运营布兰德莫尔防火墙或防火墙，旨在将极右翼排除在政府之外。在萨克森-安哈尔特州，BSW 提出如果 AfD 进入该州，将在某些问题上与 AfD 合作……

reflection.en: The projected electoral success of the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, with over 44% of the vote, represents a significant shift in the political landscape. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that when the righteous rule, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, people groan. This outcome prompts reflection on the kind of leadership that will ultimately serve the people's...
reflection.zh: 德国选择党在萨克森-安哈尔特州预测的选举成功，获得了超过44%的选票，这标志着政治格局的重大转变。《箴言》29章2节提醒我们，义人掌权，百姓喜乐；恶人掌权，百姓叹息。这一结果促使人们反思，什么样的领导才能最终服务于人民的福祉，并促进一个公正的社会。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: India's high-stakes exam system faces a crisis of trust
title.zh: 印度高风险考试制度面临信任危机

summary.en: India's National Testing Agency (NTA), established to ensure fair and standardized exams, is facing a crisis of confidence eight years after its inception due to persistent scandals like paper leaks and cheating allegations, prompting questions about whether the agency can be fixed or if the entire testing model needs...
summary.zh: 印度国家考试局（NTA）成立于八年前，旨在确保考试公平、标准化，但如今却因持续存在的泄题和作弊等丑闻而面临信任危机，引发了关于该机构是否能被修复或整个考试模式是否需要根本性改变的疑问。

body.en:
In 2017, India introduced the National Testing Agency (NTA) to conduct fair, transparent and standardised examinations.

Set up under the federal education ministry, it was meant to make exams more efficient, consistent and trustworthy, after years of paper leaks, administrative errors and cheating allegations.

Over the next few years, the agency took charge of some of India's largest and most competitive tests, including medical and engineering entrance examinations, university admissions and eligibility tests for teaching and research.

But eight years later, the organisation created to restore trust in India's exams is facing a crisis of confidence of its own.

In June, more than two million students had to retake a crucial medical entrance examination after the paper was leaked. The fallout triggered weeks of youth-led protests which eventually led to the resignation of the federal education minister.

In response, the government appointed a high-level task force led by tech tycoon Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms and restore confidence in the examination system.

A similar panel was established in 2024 after irregularities in another medical entrance examination sparked widespread unrest. That committee proposed more than 100 reforms, a little over half of which , external have reportedly been fully implemented.

The cycle has repeated: an exam goes wrong, students protest, a committee is appointed and reforms are proposed - only for another crisis to expose the same weaknesses.

Experts the BBC spoke to say the problems go beyond paper leaks - from NTA's accountability and capacity to exam centralisation, design and whether India's high-stakes testing system needs a rethink.

BJ Rao, who was part of the 2024 panel and is now head of SGT University near Delhi, says India should move more decisively towards computer-based examinations to minimise the chances of paper leaks, increase efficiency and reduce human involvement wherever possible.

"Digital connectivity has vastly improved across the country, what we need to do is put in resources and focus on upgrading infrastructure and move to computer-based exams," he told the BBC.

"We currently have ad hoc centres for conducting exams. We need to replace them with standardised state-controlled online centres."

Rao points to the NTA's reliance on contract staff: just 24 of its 221 employees are permanent, with many from bureaucratic backgrounds, according to the government.

"When you have a large portion of people who work on a temporary basis then there is no sense of belonging, and that has an impact on the functions as well. You need people who are well-versed in academia and experienced in conducting such assessments to ensure better management and oversight," he explains.

Some experts...
body.zh: 2017年，印度引入国家检测机构（NTA）进行公平、透明、规范的考试。 它是在联邦教育部的领导下设立的，其目的是在经历了多年的试卷泄露、管理错误和作弊指控后，让考试变得更加高效、一致和值得信赖。 在接下来的几年里，该机构负责了印度一些规模最大、最具竞争力的考试，包括医学和工程入学考试、大学招生以及教学和研究资格考试。 但八年后，这个为恢复人们对印度考试的信任而成立的组织本身也面临着信任危机。 6月份，试卷泄露后，超过200万学生不得不重新参加重要的医学入学考试。其后果引发了年轻人领导的为期数周的抗议活动，最终导致联邦教育部长辞职。 作为回应，政府任命了一个由科技大亨南丹·尼勒卡尼 (Nandan Nilekani) 领导的高级工作组，以建议改革并恢复对考试制度的信心。 2024 年，另一次体检中的违规行为引发了广泛的骚乱后，成立了一个类似的小组。该委员会提出了 100 多项改革，据报道其中一半多一点已得到全面实施。 这个循环不断重复：考试出错、学生抗议、任命一个委员会并提出改革建议——只是为了另一场危机暴露出同样的弱点。 BBC 采访的专家表示，问题不仅仅是试卷泄露，还包括 NTA 的责任和能力、考试集中化、设计以及印度高风险的考试系统是否需要重新考虑。 BJ Rao 是 2024 年专家组成员，现任德里附近的 SGT 大学校长，他表示印度应该更果断地转向计算机化考试，以最大限度地减少试卷泄露的可能性，提高效率并尽可能减少人为参与。 他告诉英国广播公司：“全国范围内的数字连接已经大大改善，我们需要做的是投入资源并专注于升级基础设施并转向基于计算机的考试。” “我们目前有专门的考试中心。我们需要用标准化的国家控制的在线中心取代它们。” Rao 指出 NTA 对合同工的依赖：据政府称，其 221 名员工中只有 24 名是长期雇员，其中许多人来自官僚背景。 “当你有很大一部分人是临时工作时，就会没有归属感，这也会对职能产生影响。你需要精通学术界并在进行此类评估方面经验丰富的人，以确保更好的管理和监督，”他解释道。 一些专家...

reflection.en: The establishment of the National Testing Agency (NTA) was intended to bring fairness and trust to India's high-stakes examinations. However, persistent scandals have eroded that confidence, revealing a deep need for accountability and ethical practice within the system. This situation calls for a commitment to justice, as Micah 6:8 reminds us: 'He has...
reflection.zh: 印度国家考试局（NTA）的成立旨在为高风险考试带来公平和信任。然而，持续不断的丑闻侵蚀了这种信心，暴露了该体系在问责制和道德实践方面存在深层需求。这种情况呼唤对公义的承诺，正如弥迦书6:8所提醒我们的：“世人哪，雅伟已指示你何为善。他要求你甚麽呢？无非是叫你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的雅伟同行。”

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: ‘Gigantic spaceship’: University of Bristol’s flagship £500m campus opens
title.zh: 布里斯托大学耗资5亿英镑的旗舰校区“巨型宇宙飞船”开放

summary.en: The University of Bristol's new Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus, located near the main railway station, has opened. This development aims to improve commuting for students and staff, transforming a site previously described as resembling a 'war zone' into a modern educational facility.
summary.zh: 布里斯托大学新的坦普尔码头企业园区已开放，该园区靠近主要的火车站。这一开发项目旨在改善学生和教职员工的通勤便利性，将一个曾被形容为“战争地带”的地点转变为现代化的教育设施。

As this new venture begins, it calls to mind the wisdom of committing our endeavors to a higher purpose, trusting that our plans, when dedicated, can lead to fruitful outcomes. May this campus be a place where knowledge...
reflection.zh: 坦普尔码头企业园区的开放代表着一项重大的事业，是人类智慧和规划的证明。随着这项新事业的开始，它提醒我们要将我们的努力托付于更高的目标，相信当我们奉献我们的计划时，它们可以带来丰硕的成果。愿这个校区成为知识蓬勃发展、未来得以建立的地方，并以智慧和目标为指导。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.

title.en: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
title.zh: 美代表会晤普京后与乌克兰举行会谈

summary.en: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. However, the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough, with Moscow and Kyiv remaining divided over key issues like territorial concessions.
summary.zh: 美国特使史蒂夫·维特科夫和贾里德·库什纳在基辅与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基举行了会谈，试图重振结束战争的努力。然而，最新的外交努力似乎并未取得突破，莫斯科和基辅在领土让步等关键问题上仍存在分歧。

body.en:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held "encouraging" talks in Kyiv on Sunday during their first official visit to Ukraine , but made no breakthrough toward ending Russia’s war in Ukraine . 

Despite the renewed diplomatic push, Moscow and Kyiv remain divided over key issues, particularly territorial concessions. Kushner acknowledged the challenge, saying the US was working "behind the scenes" to create the conditions for a possible deal.

As Ukraine's airspace remains closed due to the conflict, the pair arrived in Kyiv by train from Poland, having  held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin  in Moscow a day earlier.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held three rounds of talks with the US envoys, the final one joined by national security advisers from the United Kingdom, France and Germany.

After meeting with Witkoff and Kushner, Zelenskyy said the talks focused on military aid, including Patriot missile systems and other weapons Ukraine will need in the coming months. He said Kyiv was seeking "serious volumes" of US support, with backing from its European partners.

"If the war drags on until winter — and that is how things currently look — we will need a 'winter package'," he said.

The Ukrainian president also expressed gratitude that representatives of European nations were in Kyiv.

Momentum by US President Donald Trump to end the four-and-a-half-year-old conflict  has stalled in recent months after talks with Putin at the Kremlin in January failed to produce a result.

Despite hopes of a breakthrough with the Russian leader on Saturday, there were no announcements after the meeting.

Putin's foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov described the Moscow talks as constructive, frank, and useful but didn't discuss specific outcomes.

Ushakov said the talks also focused on economic issues and potentially large Russia-US projects.

During previous talks, negotiators have struggled to bring both sides together on a range of key issues, including the future of the industrial Donbas region of eastern Ukraine.

For Ukraine, hard security guarantees from its European allies and Washington are crucial to deterring Russia ​from further aggression.

Kyrylo Budanov, Zelenskyy's chief of staff, told the New York Times last weekend that he did not expect the fighting to end before spring 2027.

The war has escalated in recent months, with Putin seeking the complete conquest of Donbas and Russian drones targeting the...
body.zh: 美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳在基辅与乌克兰总统泽连斯基举行会谈，寻求重启结束战争的努力。但最新的外交努力似乎没有取得突破。 美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳周日在基辅首次正式访问乌克兰期间举行了“令人鼓舞的”会谈，但在结束俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争方面没有取得突破。 尽管新一轮的外交努力，莫斯科和基辅在关键问题上仍然存在分歧，特别是领土让步。 库什纳承认这一挑战，并表示美国正在“幕后”努力为可能达成的协议创造条件。 由于乌克兰领空因冲突而仍然关闭，两人于一天前在莫斯科与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京举行了会谈，并乘火车从波兰抵达基辅。 乌克兰总统泽伦斯基与美国特使举行了三轮会谈，英国、法国和德国的国家安全顾问参加了最后一轮会谈。 泽伦斯基在与维特科夫和库什纳会面后表示，会谈重点是军事援助，包括爱国者导弹系统和乌克兰未来几个月所需的其他武器。他表示，基辅正在寻求“大量”美国的支持，并得到欧洲伙伴的支持。 “如果战争持续到冬天——目前的情况就是这样——我们将需要一个‘冬季方案’，”他说。 乌克兰总统还对欧洲国家代表来到基辅表示感谢。 由于一月份在克里姆林宫与普京的会谈未能取得成果，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普结束这场长达四年半的冲突的势头近几个月陷入停滞。 尽管希望周六与俄罗斯领导人取得突破，但会后没有任何公告。 普京的外交政策顾问尤里·乌沙科夫称莫斯科会谈具有建设性、坦诚和有用，但没有讨论具体结果。 乌沙科夫表示，会谈还重点讨论了经济问题和潜在的俄美大型项目。 在之前的会谈中，谈判代表一直在努力让双方就一系列关键问题达成一致，其中包括乌克兰东部工业顿巴斯地区的未来。 对于乌克兰来说，其欧洲盟友和华盛顿的硬安全保证对于阻止俄罗斯进一步侵略至关重要。 泽伦斯基的幕僚长凯里洛·布达诺夫 (Kyrylo Budanov) 上周末告诉《纽约时报》，他预计战斗不会在 2027 年春季之前结束。 近几个月来，战争不断升级，普京寻求完全征服顿巴斯，俄罗斯无人机瞄准了...

reflection.en: Diplomatic efforts to end the war in Ukraine continue, with US envoys meeting President Zelenskyy. Despite "encouraging" talks, deep divisions over territorial concessions mean no breakthrough has yet occurred. The pursuit of peace is a difficult, often frustrating path, requiring persistent effort even when immediate progress is not visible.
reflection.zh: 旨在结束乌克兰战争的外交努力仍在继续，美国特使会见了泽连斯基总统。尽管进行了“令人鼓舞”的会谈，但围绕领土让步的深刻分歧意味着尚未取得突破。追求和平是一条艰难且常令人沮丧的道路，即使没有立竿见影的进展，也需要不懈的努力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Iran warns the US of 'more intense and more painful' counterattacks
title.zh: 伊朗警告美国“更激烈、更痛苦”的反击

summary.en: Iran has announced it will raise petrol prices to counter economic pressure from US sanctions. Following an exchange of fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran has warned the US that its responses to further attacks will be 'faster, more intense and more painful,' signaling an end to 'proportionate responses.' Iran...
summary.zh: 伊朗宣布将提高汽油价格以应对美国制裁的经济压力。在霍尔木兹海峡发生交火后，伊朗警告美国，其对进一步袭击的回应将是“更快、更激烈、更痛苦的”，标志着“相称性回应时代”的结束。伊朗袭击了美国的无人机、航空母舰、驱逐舰以及三艘油轮。

body.en:
Iran has warned that the "era of proportionate responses has come to an end" as it hits back against US strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.

After an exchange of fire which saw US warships and Iranian tankers targeted in the Strait, Iranian negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf warned the US that Iran will retaliate aggressively to further attacks.

He told state media that "any aggression against Iran's interests and security will receive a faster, more intense and more painful response".

"The Americans must have understood that the era of proportionate responses has come to an end."

Iran targeted a US naval drone, aircraft carrier and destroyer, and three oil tankers in the Strait — while the US Central Command said it "disabled" two Iranian oil tankers and "completely destroyed" a tanker in the Sea of Oman.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, told state media on Sunday that a "prohibited zone" will be established near the Strait of Hormuz in "the coming days".

"This zone will start from the US Navy's blockade line and include areas of the Persian Gulf," he said.

The US launched a counter-blockade on Iranian ports, a strategy it labelled "economic asphyxiation" in August.

Revolutionary Guard spokesperson Hossein Mohebi said Iran will target the US economy in response.

"If America wants to inflict one dollar of economic damage on Iran, it inflicts tens of dollars of damage on itself."

In a bid to counter US economic sanctions, Iran has announced plans to increase gasoline prices for users surpassing 110 litres per month starting Tuesday.

Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said the price of the first and second quotas, which include 110 litres, will remain unchanged, but the third quota will be raised to 100,000 Iranian rials per litre — about 4 US cents ($0.05) based on the free-market rate.

The increase in Iran's gasoline price, which is one of the lowest in the world, was discussed by the government and postponed amid concerns it could trigger new protests. Iran experienced widespread protests in 2019 over the same issue.

The higher fuel price will only affect consumers who require more than 110 litres per month and is due to "current conditions", Mohajerani said.

Other motorists can still buy up to 60 litres at 15,000 rials per litre and an additional 50 litres at 30,000 rials per litre, she added.

In December, Iran partially raised the price of its subsidised gasoline for most users, as the OPEC member sought to control rising fuel demand.

body.zh: 伊朗警告称，在反击美国在霍尔木兹海峡的袭击时，“相应反应的时代已经结束”。 在美国军舰和伊朗油轮在海峡发生交火后，伊朗谈判代表穆罕默德·巴克尔·卡利巴夫警告美国，伊朗将对进一步的袭击进行积极报复。 他对官方媒体表示，“任何侵犯伊朗利益和安全的行为都将受到更快、更强烈和更痛苦的回应”。 “美国人一定明白，相应反应的时代已经结束。” 伊朗袭击了海峡内的一架美国海军无人机、航空母舰和驱逐舰以及三艘油轮，而美国中央司令部表示，它“瘫痪”了两艘伊朗油轮，并在阿曼海“完全摧毁”了一艘油轮。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书穆赫森·礼扎伊周日对官方媒体表示，“未来几天”将在霍尔木兹海峡附近设立“禁区”。 他说：“该区域将从美国海军的封锁线开始，包括波斯湾地区。” 美国于八月对伊朗港口发起反封锁，并将这一战略称为“经济窒息”。 革命卫队发言人侯赛因·莫赫比表示，伊朗将以美国经济作为回应。 “如果美国想对伊朗造成一美元的经济损失，它就会给自己造成数十美元的损失。” 为了对抗美国的经济制裁，伊朗宣布计划从周二开始提高每月超过 110 升的用户的汽油价格。 伊朗政府发言人Fatemeh Mohajerani表示，第一和第二个配额（包括110升）的价格将保持不变，但第三个配额将提高至每升100,000伊朗里亚尔——根据自由市场汇率计算，约合4美分（0.05美元）。 伊朗汽油价格的上涨是世界上最低的国家之一，政府曾讨论过这一问题，但由于担心可能引发新的抗议活动而推迟了这一计划。 2019年，伊朗就同一问题经历了广泛的抗议。 Mohajerani 表示，由于“当前情况”，较高的燃油价格只会影响每月需求超过 110 升的消费者。 她补充说，其他驾车者仍然可以以每升 15,000 里亚尔的价格购买最多 60 升，并以每升 30,000 里亚尔的价格额外购买 50 升。 12月，伊朗部分提高了大多数用户的补贴汽油价格，因为欧佩克成员国试图控制不断增长的燃料需求。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The escalating rhetoric between Iran and the US, with Iran vowing 'more intense and more painful' responses, highlights a dangerous cycle of retaliation. The prophet Isaiah reminds us that true strength lies not in mirroring aggression, but in a higher calling: 'They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not...
reflection.zh: 伊朗和美国之间不断升级的言辞，伊朗誓言要采取“更激烈、更痛苦”的回应，这凸显了一个危险的报复循环。先知以赛亚提醒我们，真正的力量不在于模仿侵略，而在于更高的呼召：“他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。这国不举刀攻击那国，人也不再学习战事。”愿智慧胜过升级冲突的本能，引领双方走向缓和与和平。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Qantas flight makes priority landing after engine issue sparks panic over New Zealand
title.zh: 澳航航班因引擎故障紧急降落，新西兰上空引发恐慌

summary.en: Qantas has sent two engineers to Christchurch to investigate the incident. Emergency services were called to the tarmac when a Qantas flight made a priority landing in Christchurch after an engine issue, which one passenger described as 'traumatic'.
summary.zh: 澳航已派两名工程师前往基督城调查此次事件。一架澳航航班因引擎出现问题后紧急降落基督城，一名乘客称此次经历“创伤性”，紧急服务人员随即赶往停机坪。

body.en:
Emergency services were called to the tarmac when a Qantas flight made a priority landing in Christchurch after an engine issue, which one passenger described as "traumatic".

Liza-Jayne Loch was returning home from a business trip to New Zealand when the Qantas flight ran into trouble.

The plane was climbing above the scenic South Island's mountain ranges on Saturday afternoon, bound for Sydney, when a bang shook the cabin.

A passenger seated nearest the left wing soon shouted, "the engine's on fire", Loch recalled, as the cabin lights began to flicker.

Footage recorded by a passenger and shared with AAP shows flames appearing to issue from the plane's left engine in a series of rapid bursts.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"I was sitting on the left-hand side of the plane, and the flames were very, very visible," Loch said.

As the plane continued to gain altitude, Loch tried to comfort herself by recalling that modern jets could land safely on a single engine.

"That's what I kept in my head, that we could actually fly on one engine," she said.

QF122 suffered a suspected engine issue shortly after taking off from Queenstown on Saturday afternoon, before making a priority landing at Christchurch.

According to Flight Aware, the Boeing 737 landed about 52 minutes after take-off, touching down shortly before 5pm local time.

The cause of the incident has yet to be determined, but Qantas sent two engineers to Christchurch on Sunday to investigate.

Both engines are thought to have remained in operation for the duration of the flight.

Loch said conditions soon stabilised after the initial shock, while cabin staff took pains to comfort passengers.

Emergency services were waiting on the tarmac when the flight landed, and passengers were allowed to disembark as normal after a short wait.

A Qantas spokesperson said the plane was believed to have suffered an engine issue and steps would be taken to support affected customers.

"Our pilots are highly trained to manage situations like this and the aircraft landed safely," they said.

"We know this would have been a distressing experience for passengers and will be contacting all customers to provide support."

Affected passengers were put up in a hotel near the Christchurch International Airport before being booked on a complimentary flight to Sydney on Sunday.

While the second flight went off without a hitch, Loch said nerves were still high.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 当澳洲航空的一架航班在发动机出现问题后优先降落在基督城时，紧急服务人员被呼叫到停机坪，一名乘客称这是“创伤性的”。 丽莎-杰恩·洛克 (Liza-Jayne Loch) 正在从新西兰出差回家时，澳洲航空的航班遇到了麻烦。 周六下午，这架飞机正在风景秀丽的南岛山脉上空爬升，飞往悉尼，突然一声巨响震动了机舱。 洛赫回忆说，当机舱灯光开始闪烁时，坐在最靠近左翼的一名乘客很快就喊道：“发动机着火了”。 一名乘客录制并与 AAP 分享的视频显示，火焰似乎从飞机的左侧发动机中快速喷出。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “我坐在飞机的左侧，火焰非常非常明显，”洛克说。 随着飞机继续上升，洛克试图安慰自己，回忆起现代喷气式飞机可以通过单引擎安全着陆。 “这就是我一直牢记在心的事情，我们实际上可以用一台发动机来飞行，”她说。 QF122 周六下午从皇后镇起飞后不久就疑似出现发动机问题，随后优先降落在基督城。 据 Flight Aware 报道，这架波音 737 飞机在起飞后约 52 分钟着陆，在当地时间下午 5 点前不久着陆。 事件原因尚未确定，但澳洲航空已于周日派出两名工程师前往基督城进行调查。 据信，这两个发动机在飞行期间一直保持运转。 洛克表示，在最初的震惊之后，情况很快就稳定下来，而机舱工作人员则煞费苦心地安抚乘客。 航班降落时，紧急服务人员正在停机坪上等待，短暂等待后，乘客被允许正常下机。 澳航发言人表示，据信这架飞机出现了发动机问题，将采取措施支持受影响的客户。 他们说：“我们的飞行员训练有素，能够应对此类情况，飞机安全着陆。” “我们知道这对乘客来说将是一次痛苦的经历，我们将联系所有乘客提供支持。” 受影响的乘客被安置在基督城国际机场附近的一家酒店，然后被预订周日飞往悉尼的免费航班。 洛克表示，虽然第二次航班顺利起飞，但人们仍然高度紧张。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The sudden fear and trauma experienced by passengers on the Qantas flight highlight how quickly our sense of security can be shattered. In moments of unexpected crisis, the heart can feel broken by fear and uncertainty. Yet, even in such distress, there is a divine promise of healing and restoration for those who are hurting.
reflection.zh: 澳航航班上乘客突如其来的恐惧和创伤，凸显了我们的安全感可以多么迅速地被打破。在意想不到的危机时刻，心灵会因恐惧和不确定而感到破碎。然而，即使在这种痛苦中，对于那些受伤的心灵，也有着神圣的医治与修复的应许。

verse.textEn: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verse.textZh: 他医好伤心的人，裹好他们的伤处。

title.en: US diplomats to announce 'substantive plans' after peace talks with Moscow and Kyiv
title.zh: 美国外交官宣布与莫斯科和基辅和谈后的“实质性计划”

summary.en: US diplomats are set to announce 'substantive plans' in the coming weeks following peace talks with Moscow and Kyiv. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope for an agreement with the US delegation, though he indicated the war with Russia was likely to continue in the short term.
summary.zh: 美国外交官将在与莫斯科和基辅进行和平谈判后，在未来几周内宣布“实质性计划”。乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示希望与美国代表团达成协议，但他同时指出，与俄罗斯的战争在短期内可能会继续。

body.en:
Despite the latest push from the United States to speak to the leaders of Russia and Ukraine in their respective capitals, a breakthrough in peace negotiations appears no closer.

The US delegation said that "substantive plans will be announced in the coming weeks" during its stay in Moscow.

However, war with Russia "at the moment" looked likely to continue into the coming months, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday, after talks with the envoys in Kyiv.

US envoy Steve Witkoff and Zelenskyy both gave upbeat assessments of the talks, but neither announced any breakthroughs on ending the war with Russia.

Witkoff, who is President Donald Trump's business ally, and Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, travelled to Kyiv a day after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow — the latest of several visits to the city.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Sunday's trip to Kyiv was their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, which has been hit by deadly Russian strikes for more than four years.

Zelenskyy said: "We very much hope that we will be able to reach agreements with our American partners, and we are counting on the support of our European partners if the war continues in winter — and this is how it appears at the moment."

Zelenskyy also said that Ukraine would hold talks with the US, France and Germany, but did not elaborate.

The Ukrainian leader, who has previously called for a meeting with Putin, reiterated his call that only a meeting between leaders could resolve territorial issues.

Moscow occupies large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine, and the Kremlin told the Americans Saturday it was feeling "confident" it would advance more.

Moscow has said it wants not just the territories it occupies but the land it claims as Russian to be recognised as its own — terms unacceptable to Kyiv.

"We've had a very meaningful discussion, substantive, important, and we are very encouraged and we look forward to continuing this as long as it takes."

Kushner added: "Hopefully this trip has come out with some new ways to advance forward. I think we've learned a lot from the trip."

Witkoff and Kushner travelled to the region hoping to revive the Trump administration's push for peace in Europe's worst conflict since World War II, after a summer of escalation.

Another round of talks in the presence of British, French and German representatives was still ongoing.

Zelenskyy said he was grateful the Europeans were there, adding: "Here we are all on the same side."

Like all visiting officials, the American delegation had arrived by train, with "Peace Express" written on the platform at Kyiv Central...
body.zh: 尽管美国最近敦促俄罗斯和乌克兰领导人在各自首都进行对话，但和平谈判似乎并未取得突破。 美国代表团表示，在莫斯科逗留期间“将在未来几周内宣布实质性计划”。 然而，乌克兰总统泽连斯基周日在基辅与特使会谈后表示，“目前”与俄罗斯的战争可能会持续到未来几个月。 美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和泽伦斯基都对会谈做出了乐观评价，但都没有宣布在结束与俄罗斯的战争方面取得任何突破。 唐纳德·特朗普总统的商业盟友维特科夫和特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳在莫斯科会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京一天后前往基辅，这是多次访问该市的最新一次。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 周日的基辅之行是他们第一次访问乌克兰首都，四年多来，这里一直遭受俄罗斯的致命袭击。 泽连斯基表示：“我们非常希望能够与美国伙伴达成协议，如果战争在冬季继续下去，我们也指望欧洲伙伴的支持——目前的情况就是这样。” 泽连斯基还表示，乌克兰将与美国、法国和德国举行会谈，但没有详细说明。 这位此前曾呼吁与普京会晤的乌克兰领导人重申，只有领导人之间的会晤才能解决领土问题。 莫斯科占领了乌克兰东部和南部的大片地区，克里姆林宫周六告诉美国人，它“有信心”会取得更大进展。 莫斯科表示，它不仅希望其占领的领土得到承认，还希望其声称属于俄罗斯的土地被承认为自己的土地——这是基辅无法接受的条件。 “我们进行了一次非常有意义的讨论，实质性的、重要的，我们深受鼓舞，我们期待着尽可能长时间地继续下去。” 库什纳补充道：“希望这次访问能够带来一些新的前进方式。我认为我们从这次访问中学到了很多东西。” 维特科夫和库什纳前往该地区，希望在经历了一个夏天的冲突升级后，恢复特朗普政府在欧洲自二战以来最严重的冲突中推动和平的努力。 英国、法国和德国代表出席的另一轮会谈仍在进行中。 泽伦斯基表示，他很感激欧洲人在那里，并补充道：“在这里我们都站在同一边。” 与所有来访官员一样，美国代表团是乘坐火车抵达的，基辅中央火车站的站台上写着“和平快车”……

reflection.en: As US diplomats announce 'substantive plans' following talks with Moscow and Kyiv, we are reminded of the difficult and often protracted work of peacemaking. The pursuit of peace, even when breakthroughs are not immediate, is a calling to overcome conflict with dialogue and diplomacy, reflecting the beatitude for those who work for peace.
reflection.zh: 随着美国外交官在与莫斯科和基辅会谈后宣布“实质性计划”，我们被提醒和平建设工作是艰难且常常旷日持久的。追求和平，即使突破并非立竿见影，也是一种呼召，要以对话和外交来化解冲突，这体现了那些致力于和平者的福分。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
title.zh: 德国、科索沃联手对抗携带致命病毒的蜱虫

summary.en: Germany, with its high-security laboratories, and Kosovo, with its experience and presence of Hyalomma ticks, are joining forces. Scientists from both nations are collaborating to fight the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever and the ticks that transmit it.
summary.zh: 德国拥有高安全级别的实验室，而科索沃则有携带致命的克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒的巨猎蝽（Hyalomma ticks）及其传播经验。两国科学家正携手合作，共同对抗这种致命疾病及其传播媒介。

body.en:
Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

It can spot its prey from up to 200 meters (about 650 feet) away — but unlike many of its fellow species, it doesn't lurk in the grass waiting for its victim to come closer. Instead it runs after it, chasing animals and humans alike.

The Hyalomma tick, often called "the great hunting tick," was previously found mostly in Africa, Asia, and southern Europe. But climate change means it can now survive further north and it has already been spotted in Germany and various Eastern European countries. Kosovo, in southeastern Europe, has been a hot spot for the tick for some time now.

The Hyalomma tick is also a vector of the highly pathogenic virus for Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, a potentially deadly disease with a high fatality rate. Symptoms of the disease are comparable to those of Ebola fever or the Marburg virus . These are capable of destroying blood and lymphatic vessels, which can lead to internal bleeding and death.

Kurtesh Sherifi first read about Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in the newspaper in 2005, when he was completing his studies as a veterinarian in Berlin. The article said that 11 people in his homeland, Kosovo, had contracted the disease and five had died. He was already interested in pathogens that can be transmitted between animals and humans, known as zoonoses, and Crimean-Congo fever intrigued him.

Back home, Sherifi started work with the faculty of agriculture and veterinary medicine at the University of Pristina. But the budget for research was tight. Kosovo, a small country with only about 1.6 million citizens, didn't have a high-security laboratory or the equipment necessary for investigating the Crimean-Congo fever virus.

Sherifi got in touch with Germany's largest institution for study in this area, the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine in Hamburg. 

One of the researchers was Petra Emmerich, a virologist and expert on what are known as Risk Group 4 viruses — viruses that cause severe, often fatal, diseases and usually have no widely available treatment. The Crimean-Congo virus is in that risk group.

Emmerich also acts as a reservist in the German military, which is especially interested in viruses that could be used as biological weapons. She was sent to Kosovo in 2009, which is when she met Sherifi.

A lively exchange began between the researchers. In Kosovo, a structure was established to monitor the spread of the Hyalomma tick and the virus . In 2013, the researchers' joint work began to receive funding through the German Biosecurity Program,...
body.zh: 德国拥有高度安全的实验室，而科索沃则拥有玻璃蜱，并经历过致命的克里米亚-刚果出血热。德国和科索沃科学家共同努力对抗这种疾病及其传播媒介。 它可以在 200 米（约 650 英尺）外发现猎物，但与许多同类不同的是，它不会潜伏在草丛中等待猎物靠近。相反，它会追赶它，追逐动物和人类。 透明蜱通常被称为“伟大的狩猎蜱”，以前主要发现于非洲、亚洲和南欧。但气候变化意味着它现在可以在更北的地方生存，并且已经在德国和多个东欧国家发现了它。一段时间以来，位于欧洲东南部的科索沃一直是蜱虫的热点地区。 玻璃蜱也是克里米亚-刚果出血热高致病性病毒的载体，克里米亚-刚果出血热是一种潜在致命的疾病，死亡率很高。该疾病的症状与埃博拉热或马尔堡病毒的症状相似。它们能够破坏血液和淋巴管，从而导致内出血和死亡。 Kurtesh Sherifi 第一次在报纸上看到克里米亚-刚果出血热是在 2005 年，当时他正在柏林完成兽医学业。文章称，他的祖国科索沃已有11人感染该病，其中5人死亡。他已经对可以在动物和人类之间传播的病原体（称为人畜共患病）感兴趣，克里米亚-刚果热引起了他的兴趣。 回到家乡后，谢里菲开始在普里什蒂纳大学农业和兽医学院工作。但研究预算很紧张。科索沃是一个只有约 160 万公民的小国，没有高度安全的实验室，也没有调查克里米亚-刚果热病毒所需的设备。 谢里菲联系了德国该领域最大的研究机构——汉堡的伯恩哈德·诺赫特热带医学研究所。 其中一位研究人员是佩特拉·埃默里奇 (Petra Emmerich)，他是一位病毒学家，也是“风险组 4”病毒方面的专家。这种病毒会导致严重且往往致命的疾病，并且通常没有广泛可用的治疗方法。克里米亚-刚果病毒属于该风险组。 艾默里奇还是德国军队的预备役军人，他们对可用作生物武器的病毒特别感兴趣。 2009 年，她被派往科索沃，那时她遇到了谢里菲。 研究人员之间开始了热烈的交流。科索沃建立了一个机构来监测玻璃蜱和病毒的传播。 2013年，研究人员的联合工作开始通过德国生物安全计划获得资助，...

reflection.en: The 'great hunting tick,' capable of pursuing prey, presents a formidable challenge. Yet, human ingenuity, spurred by the need to protect life, finds a way. By observing creation's details, as Job 12:7 encourages, scientists in Germany and Kosovo are pooling their knowledge to combat this threat, demonstrating a shared human endeavor to understand and...
reflection.zh: 这种被称为“大猎蝽”的蜱虫，能够追逐猎物，构成严峻的挑战。然而，人类的智慧，在保护生命的需要驱动下，找到了应对之道。正如约伯记12:7所鼓励的，通过观察受造界的细节，德国和科索沃的科学家正在汇集他们的知识来对抗这一威胁，这展示了人类为理解和减轻来自自然界的危险而进行的共同努力。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: How climate change and food insecurity could fuel future conflicts
title.zh: 气候变化和粮食不安全可能加剧未来冲突

summary.en: Climate change, conflict, and trade tensions are straining the global food system. New research indicates that the primary risk lies not in food shortages themselves, but in societies' ability to adapt peacefully to these changes. Extreme weather events and ongoing wars are disrupting food supplies and supply chains,...
summary.zh: 气候变化、冲突和贸易紧张局势正在给全球粮食系统带来压力。新的研究表明，最大的风险并非粮食短缺本身，而是社会能否和平地适应变化。极端天气事件和持续的战争正在扰乱粮食供应和供应链，并可能导致冲突加剧。

body.en:
Climate change, conflict, and trade tensions are putting pressure on the global food system. New research suggests the biggest risk is not food shortages, but whether societies can peacefully adapt to change.

The world's food system is under growing stress, and new research is pointing to areas where this could lead to conflict.

Severe droughts and extreme weather are damaging harvests in many regions. A developing El Niño event is even threatening to worsen food shortages for millions of people next year. At the same time, wars and geopolitical tensions are disrupting supply chains that keep food and farm supplies moving.

The war in Ukraine has repeatedly shaken grain markets , while the Iran war's impact on the Strait of Hormuz has driven up fuel and fertilizer prices , increasing costs for farmers everywhere. 

Experts have long warned that rising food insecurity could fuel instability. When people can no longer feed their families, they argue over land, water, and other resources — or they move. In fragile countries, these pressures can contribute to social unrest and even armed conflict.

Now, new research has suggested where some of these risks are greatest. The  Climate-Driven Agricultural Decline Index (CADI) , developed by Laura Mayoral, Hannes Mueller and colleagues, maps how climate change is reshaping agricultural productivity around the world. "The heaviest losses are in the tropical regions," said Mueller, a researcher at the Institute for Economic Analysis and the Barcelona School of Economics.

Climate change is already reducing food production in many parts of the world. Hundreds of millions of people live in areas where harvests are smaller than 30 years ago. Mueller mentioned Australia, Argentina, Moldova, Nigeria, Romania, the United States, and Sudan as countries where agricultural losses are already being felt.

"Northern Africa is another region we should pay much more attention to. If you look at the map, it just looks terrible. It really looks horrible," he said. 

And climate change is only one part of the story. Wars, trade disruptions, export bans, and rising fertilizer costs can magnify food insecurity.

Within the next 25 years, nearly half of the world's people could be living in areas where farms are producing less food.

These pressures can undermine governments, help cause migration , and make it easier for armed groups to recruit fighters. In societies that are already unstable, such factors can push them toward crisis. 

Yet CADI's research points to a surprising reality: Gains in agricultural productivity also appear to increase the risk of violence. Mueller said the key issue is not just scarcity, but change. The climate crisis and other shocks do not simply...
body.zh: 气候变化、冲突和贸易紧张局势给全球粮食系统带来压力。新研究表明，最大的风险不是食物短缺，而是社会能否和平地适应变化。 世界粮食系统面临着越来越大的压力，新的研究指出这可能会导致冲突。 严重干旱和极端天气正在损害许多地区的收成。正在发展的厄尔尼诺现象甚至有可能加剧明年数百万人的粮食短缺。与此同时，战争和地缘政治紧张局势正在扰乱维持粮食和农产品供应的供应链。 乌克兰战争一再震动粮食市场，伊朗战争对霍尔木兹海峡的影响推高了燃料和化肥价格，增加了各地农民的成本。 专家长期以来一直警告说，粮食不安全加剧可能会加剧不稳定。当人们无法再养家糊口时，他们就会为了土地、水和其他资源而争论，或者搬家。在脆弱国家，这些压力可能导致社会动荡甚至武装冲突。 现在，新的研究表明其中一些风险最大的地方。由 Laura Mayoral、Hannes Mueller 及其同事开发的气候驱动农业衰退指数 (CADI) 描绘了气候变化如何重塑世界各地的农业生产力。 “损失最严重的是热带地区，”经济分析研究所和巴塞罗那经济学院的研究员穆勒说。 气候变化已经导致世界许多地区的粮食产量减少。数亿人生活在收成低于 30 年前的地区。穆勒提到澳大利亚、阿根廷、摩尔多瓦、尼日利亚、罗马尼亚、美国和苏丹都是已经感受到农业损失的国家。 “北非是另一个我们应该更加关注的地区。如果你看看地图，它看起来很糟糕。它看起来真的很可怕，”他说。 气候变化只是故事的一部分。战争、贸易中断、出口禁令和化肥成本上涨可能会加剧粮食不安全。 未来 25 年内，世界上近一半的人口可能生活在农场粮食产量减少的地区。 这些压力可能会削弱政府，导致移民，并使武装团体更容易招募战士。在已经不稳定的社会中，这些因素可能会将其推向危机。 然而，CADI 的研究指出了一个令人惊讶的现实：农业生产力的提高似乎也增加了暴力风险。穆勒表示，关键问题不仅仅是稀缺，还有变化。气候危机和其他冲击不仅仅......

reflection.en: The world's food system is facing unprecedented pressure from climate change and geopolitical instability. As research suggests, the greatest challenge is not merely scarcity, but our collective capacity for peaceful adaptation. In times of such global stress, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a present help in times of trouble.
reflection.zh: 世界粮食系统正面临气候变化和地缘政治不稳定的前所未有的压力。研究表明，最大的挑战不仅仅是短缺，更是我们集体和平适应的能力。在如此全球性的压力时期，《诗篇》46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是患难中随时的帮助。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Ebola: Why children are last to be treated in medical crises
title.zh: 埃博拉：为何儿童在医疗危机中最后得到治疗

summary.en: In the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, children are more likely to die than adults. This is not always due to the disease itself, but often because specific medicines for younger patients are harder to obtain, leading to a mortality rate of over 60% for children under 5.
summary.zh: 在刚果民主共和国最新的埃博拉疫情中，儿童比成人死亡的可能性更大。但这并非总是由于疾病本身，而是因为针对年轻患者的特效药物往往更难获得，导致5岁以下儿童的死亡率超过60%。

body.en:
In the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, children are more likely to die than adults. But it's not always due to the disease. Specific medicines for younger people are often harder to come by.

The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been devastating. Since the outbreak began in mid-May, more than 3,000 people have died.

Almost half of people infected with Ebola are expected to die, and the mortality rate is particularly high for young children. According to a commentary by Doctors Without Borders recently published in medical journal The Lancet , the mortality rate for children under the age of 5 is over 60% .

But often, it's because of a lack of medication and information on how to use it with young patients, rather than then disease itself.

"Children must be centered in Ebola treatment and prevention research," the aid organization wrote in early September .

At the heart of the debate is the EBO-PEP study, which began mid-July. The study looks at an experimental antiviral drug called obeldesivir, which is being studied for its ability to protect people exposed to the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, the strain responsible for the current deadly outbreak .

But children weighing less than 30 kilograms (about 66 pounds) and around 12 years old or younger, were not included in the original study. But that could change soon with protocols to include children weighing over 20 kilograms.

Children weighing less than 20 kilograms — that is, roughly 6 years old or younger — won't be included in the treatment. There is an alternative treatment for them: Another antiviral drug, remdesivir, given intravenously. But as Doctors Without Borders argued, a 10-day course of infusions is difficult to administer during an outbreak, especially for young children.

According to Neal Russell, a pediatric doctor based in London who consults for Doctors Without Borders and who was also the lead author of the Lancet commentary, young children are at particularly high risk from Ebola . This could be due to their weakened immune systems, underlying health conditions, or the fact that treating them for Ebola is especially challenging in an outbreak.

For example, children are often harder to diagnose than adults because early symptoms resemble other illnesses, and young children often find it difficult to describe their symptoms accurately. Other issues include the fact that children cannot always be accompanied into an Ebola treatment center by their parents or caregivers, something that is especially important in their recovery. Younger Ebola patients also require closer monitoring and specially trained staff.

In May, an American doctor was treated at Berlin's Charite hospital after contracting the...
body.zh: 在刚果民主共和国最近爆发的埃博拉疫情中，儿童比成人更有可能死亡。但这并不总是由疾病引起的。针对年轻人的特定药物通常更难获得。 目前刚果民主共和国爆发的埃博拉疫情是毁灭性的。自5月中旬疫情爆发以来，已有3000多人死亡。 预计几乎一半感染埃博拉病毒的人会死亡，其中幼儿的死亡率尤其高。根据无国界医生组织最近在医学杂志《柳叶刀》上发表的评论，5岁以下儿童的死亡率超过60%。 但通常，这是因为缺乏药物和如何对年轻患者使用药物的信息，而不是疾病本身。 “儿童必须以埃博拉治疗和预防研究为中心，”该援助组织在九月初写道。 争论的核心是 7 月中旬开始的 EBO-PEP 研究。这项研究着眼于一种名为奥贝地西韦的实验性抗病毒药物，该药物正在研究其保护暴露于本迪布焦埃博拉病毒（本迪布焦埃博拉病毒）的人的能力，该病毒株是当前致命疫情的罪魁祸首。 但体重低于 30 公斤（约 66 磅）且年龄在 12 岁或以下的儿童并未包括在最初的研究中。但随着协议将体重超过 20 公斤的儿童纳入其中，这种情况可能很快就会改变。 体重低于 20 公斤的儿童（即大约 6 岁或以下）不会参与治疗。他们有另一种治疗方法：另一种抗病毒药物瑞德西韦，静脉注射。但正如无国界医生组织所言，在疫情爆发期间，为期 10 天的输液过程很难实施，尤其是对于年幼的儿童。 伦敦儿科医生尼尔·拉塞尔（Neal Russell）为无国界医生组织提供咨询，也是《柳叶刀》评论的主要作者，他表示，幼儿感染埃博拉病毒的风险特别高。这可能是因为他们的免疫系统较弱、潜在的健康状况不佳，或者在埃博拉疫情爆发时治疗他们的埃博拉病毒尤其具有挑战性。 例如，儿童通常比成人更难诊断，因为早期症状类似于其他疾病，而且幼儿常常发现很难准确描述他们的症状。其他问题包括儿童不能总是由父母或护理人员陪同进入埃博拉治疗中心，这对于他们的康复尤为重要。年轻的埃博拉患者还需要更密切的监测和经过专门培训的工作人员。 五月，一名美国医生在柏林慈善医院接受治疗后感染了...

reflection.en: The report from the Democratic Republic of Congo reveals a heartbreaking reality: children under 5 face a mortality rate over 60% in the current Ebola outbreak. This disproportionate suffering stems not just from the virus, but from the scarcity of age-specific treatments. It calls us to advocate for the most vulnerable, ensuring that every life, no matter...
reflection.zh: 刚果民主共和国的报道揭示了一个令人心碎的现实：在当前的埃博拉疫情中，5岁以下儿童的死亡率超过60%。这种不成比例的痛苦不仅源于病毒本身，也源于针对特定年龄段的治疗药物的匮乏。这呼吁我们为最脆弱的群体发声，确保每一个生命，无论多么年幼，都能得到其迫切需要的照护。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: The US now has access to more than half Australia’s military bases – could it drag the country unwillingly into war?
title.zh: 美国现在可以进入澳大利亚一半以上的军事基地——这是否可能将该国不情愿地拖入战争？

summary.en: Exclusive reports reveal that US-controlled weapons corporations and forces have control or access to over 100 facilities across Australia. Some analysts liken this extensive presence to a 'colonisation' of Australia's military capabilities, with new data mapping the significant US militarisation on Australian soil.
summary.zh: 独家报道披露，美国控制的武器公司和部队在澳大利亚拥有超过100个设施的控制权或使用权。一些分析人士将这种广泛的存在比作对澳大利亚军事力量的“殖民化”，新的数据显示了澳大利亚本土美国军事化的程度。

body.en: Exclusive: US-controlled weapons corporations and forces have control or access to more than 100 facilities across the continent, which some analysts describe as a ‘colonisation’ of Australia’s military. Find a map of them here US military presence in Australia, mapped – video Why can the US access so many Australian military bases? – podcast US military interests control or have access to more than 100 defence facilities on Australian soil, in what some analysts describe as a “saturation” – even a “colonisation” – of the Australian continent. New data compiled by the Nautilus Institute and published by Guardian Australia maps the extent of US militarisation. The US military controls 17 facilities on mainland Australia and has access to 75 more Australian-run military installations. US defence corporations have access to an additional 18. Gathering intelligence, accessing satellite data for targeting information and communications intercepts. Training, including for 2,500 marines on dry-season rotation in the Northern Territory. Pre-positioning warfighting assets such as Osprey aircraft. Logistics hubs holding weapons, munitions and fuel, stored in case of a war in the Pacific. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：美国控制的武器公司和部队控制或进入了整个非洲大陆的 100 多个设施，一些分析人士将其描述为澳大利亚军队的“殖民化”。在这里找到它们的地图 美国在澳大利亚的军事存在，已绘制 - 视频 为什么美国可以进入如此多的澳大利亚军事基地？ – 播客 美国军事利益集团控制或有权使用澳大利亚领土上的 100 多个防御设施，一些分析人士将其描述为澳大利亚大陆的“饱和”，甚至是“殖民化”。鹦鹉螺研究所编制并由澳大利亚卫报发布的新数据绘制了美国军事化的程度。美国军方控制着澳大利亚大陆的 17 个设施，并有权使用另外 75 个澳大利亚管理的军事设施。美国国防公司可以使用额外的 18 个卫星数据来收集情报、访问卫星数据以进行目标信息和通信拦截。训练，包括为 2,500 名海军陆战队员在北领地进行旱季轮换训练。预先部署鱼鹰飞机等作战资产。储存武器、弹药和燃料的后勤中心，以防太平洋发生战争。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The extensive US military presence across Australia, with access to over 100 facilities, raises profound questions about national sovereignty and the potential for entanglement in distant conflicts. Isaiah's vision of nations beating swords into plowshares offers a counterpoint, a hope for a world where military might is transformed into instruments of...
reflection.zh: 美国在澳大利亚广泛的军事存在，拥有超过100个设施的使用权，引发了关于国家主权和卷入遥远冲突的潜在问题的深刻疑问。以赛亚关于列国将刀打成犁头的异象提供了一个对照，一个关于军事力量被转化为和平与生产力工具的世界的希望。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: EU faces 300,000 factory job cuts as China ‘colonises’ supply chains, industry warns

Eurometal forecasts 300,000 manufacturing job losses by the end of 2026 due to escalating competition from China, which...
